`Checkbox.Indicator` is cut. CSS on the input (`appearance: none`, `:checked`, `[data-indeterminate]`), an element of the developer beside the input (`:checked + .icon`), or the `element` slot with `state` gives the mark.

The file tests the id of React 17, which has no `useId`. Vue gives each part an id with `useId`.

The part is the native input. The browser gives the role, the checked state, the disabled state and the required state (rules 8.1, 8.3).
The part writes no `id` on a label of the developer. A native label names its input, and a `Field.Label` names the input with `for`.

`Checkbox` is the part: one `<input type="checkbox">` (rules 8.1, 8.3). The flat types `CheckboxProps`, `CheckboxState` and `CheckboxChangeEventReason` replace the namespace types. `readonly` replaces `readOnly`. `form` is a plain attribute, and the `element` of the template ref replaces `inputRef`. The input has no `data-checked`, `data-unchecked`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-readonly` or `data-invalid`: CSS selects `:checked`, `:disabled`, `:required`, `[aria-readonly]` and `[aria-invalid]`.
